title: Inside a Guitar Case
description: Look closely at a guitar through its familiar parts and the actions used to make sound.
cardDescription: Look closely at a guitar through its familiar parts and the actions used to make sound.
focus: The clues identify objects by location or purpose. A part of the instrument differs from the action performed on it.
solvingTip: Look for a support, a string-related part, or a playing action.
words: String instrument with a neck and a sound-producing body
Taut length that vibrates when a guitar is played
Raised strip across a guitar neck marking a note position
Long part of a guitar supporting the fingerboard
Large lower part of a guitar
Guitar part supporting strings near the lower end
Small flat tool used to pluck a guitar string
To sweep across several guitar strings
To pull and release one string to make sound
Group of notes sounded together on a guitar
To adjust guitar strings to the desired pitches
Small turning part used to tighten or loosen a string
Protective container fitted for a guitar
Band supporting a guitar from the player’s shoulder

answerNotes.FRET: A fret helps mark a string’s sounding length. The clue names a physical strip rather than the verb meaning worry.
answerNotes.BRIDGE: Bridge is an instrument part here. It supports the strings rather than crossing a river.
answerNotes.PICK: A guitar pick is a small plucking tool. It is separate from the fingertip that may also pluck a string.
answerNotes.CHORD: A chord contains notes sounded together. A melody instead follows notes in sequence.

title: Brass Band Sounds
description: Meet familiar brass instruments and the parts that shape their sound.
cardDescription: Meet familiar brass instruments and the parts that shape their sound.
focus: These clues describe instrument shapes and sound-making parts. A piece of equipment can have a familiar everyday name.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a whole instrument, a moving part, or an opening.
words: Brass instrument often played with three valves
Brass instrument commonly using a long movable slide
Coiled brass instrument with a flared bell
Compact brass instrument related to the trumpet
Instrument family sounded by vibrating the player’s lips
Moving device redirecting air through an instrument’s tubing
Movable tubing used to change a trombone’s pitch
Flared open end of a brass instrument
Part against which a brass player places the lips
Part of the mouth vibrated to play a brass instrument
Gas blown into a wind instrument
Device inserted into or held near a brass bell to alter sound
Group that may combine brass and percussion instruments

answerNotes.BELL: Bell names the flared opening here. It does not mean a separate ringing percussion instrument.
answerNotes.MUTE: A brass mute changes the sound. It is a physical device rather than a television’s silence setting.
answerNotes.SLIDE: The trombone slide changes the instrument’s effective tube length. The clue asks for the moving part.
answerNotes.VALVE: A valve redirects the air path. It differs from the opening called the bell.

title: Woodwinds and Their Voices
description: Explore familiar woodwind names and the small parts used to shape their tones.
cardDescription: Explore familiar woodwind names and the small parts used to shape their tones.
focus: The clues describe a family of instruments whose members can be made from different materials. Some use reeds, while others do not.
solvingTip: Use the whole-instrument clues to cross the shorter parts and sound words.
words: Woodwind commonly played across an opening without a reed
Single-reed woodwind with a largely straight body
Large low double-reed instrument with folded tubing
Usually metal woodwind played with a single reed
Thin vibrating strip used in many woodwind mouthpieces
Lever used to open or close an instrument’s tone hole
Opening in an instrument’s tube that affects pitch
Hollow body through which a wind instrument’s air travels
Air expelled by the player to make a wind sound
Instrument-family name including flutes and clarinets
Small high-pitched relative of the flute
Protective fitted container for a woodwind instrument
Musical sound with a particular quality

answerNotes.WOODWIND: Woodwind is a family name rather than a promise about material. A metal saxophone still belongs to this family.
answerNotes.REED: A reed is a vibrating strip. Flutes produce sound differently and do not need a reed.
answerNotes.PICCOLO: A piccolo is a small flute relative. Its size is associated with a higher pitch range.
answerNotes.KEY: Key names a mechanical lever here. It does not mean a musical key signature in this clue.

title: A Beat from the Drum Kit
description: Explore a drum kit through familiar striking tools, surfaces, and rhythm words.
cardDescription: Explore a drum kit through familiar striking tools, surfaces, and rhythm words.
focus: The clues distinguish complete instruments from their parts. Sound and shape provide direct routes to the answers.
solvingTip: Look for a striking tool, a drum surface, a pedal-operated item, or an action.
words: Percussion instrument with a stretched vibrating surface
Drum with rattling wires stretched beneath a head
Word before drum for a kit’s large low-pitched instrument
Round metal percussion plate struck for a ringing sound
Pair of cymbals commonly operated with a foot pedal
Slender implement used to strike a drum
Wire or fiber tool used for a softer drum sound
Foot-operated lever used in a drum kit
Regular musical pulse followed by a drummer
Rapid repeated drum strokes producing a sustained sound
Outer ring around a drum’s head
Stretched membrane forming a drum’s striking surface
Collection of drums and cymbals played together
Handheld percussion instrument with jingling metal disks

answerNotes.SNARE: The snare drum has wires that rattle against a head. That feature creates its characteristic crisp sound.
answerNotes.HIHAT: Hi-hat is normally written with a hyphen. The grid combines its letters into one entry.
answerNotes.HEAD: A drumhead is the stretched vibrating surface. The clue uses head for an instrument part.
answerNotes.ROLL: A drum roll uses rapidly repeated strokes. It does not describe a bread item or a turning wheel here.

title: Bellows and Buttons
description: Explore an accordion and its relatives through familiar parts and the movements that supply air.
cardDescription: Explore an accordion and its relatives through familiar parts and the movements that supply air.
focus: The clues identify free-reed instruments and their physical parts. Everyday action words help explain how the instrument changes shape.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue describes the whole instrument, its air supply, or a control.
words: Portable free-reed instrument played with bellows and keys or buttons
Folding chamber that moves air through an accordion
Small pressed control on many accordions
Piano-like control on one type of accordion
Vibrating strip producing an accordion’s tone
Gas moved through an accordion by its bellows
Band helping support a carried accordion
One pleat in an accordion’s expanding chamber
To open the bellows farther apart
Small free-reed instrument with bellows between two ends
Body part operating one side of an accordion
Container protecting an accordion between performances
Melody that can be played on an accordion

answerNotes.BELLOWS: Bellows move air as they expand and compress. They are the flexible chamber rather than the keys or buttons.
answerNotes.CONCERTINA: A concertina has bellows between its ends. Its compact form distinguishes it from many larger accordions.
answerNotes.REED: Accordion reeds vibrate in moving air. The word names a sound-producing part rather than a wetland plant here.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button is a musical control in this clue. It does not fasten a garment.
